## 2. Face2Social: Best for Connecting Photos to Popular Social Media Profiles

Face2Social is an image lookup tool that locates social media accounts using certain photos.

Compared to PimEyes, which skips social platforms entirely, Face2Social has access to popular social media accounts, such as TikTok and X.

Face2Social users can register and search for matches for free, but viewing full handles or direct profile links requires a paid monthly plan.

 $19.99 for 10 reports.
 $199.99 for 200 reports.

Although its focus is narrower than general reverse lookup tools, Face2Social can flag impersonation, reused social identities, and widely shared content.

Test Results: Face2Social found 80 (accurate) matches from 4 major social media platforms. [...] ## 6. FaceSeek: Best for Searching Edited, Cropped, and Compressed Photos

FaceSeek is a face search engine you can use to reverse search edited, compressed, or low-quality photos.

FaceSeek scans public web pages, blogs, articles, Pinterest, YouTube, social media, and more, but some results require manual verification.

It returns tons of matches for free, with access to sources for low prices ($1.99, $9.90, $17.90, and $29.90).

Test Results: FaceSeek found 96 accurate matches; 73 were from social media.

## 7. EyeMatch.ai: Best for Tracking a Photo’s Digital Footprint

EyeMatch.ai is an AI face search engine that displays visual matches in a chronological timeline. [...] Google Lens is a free visual search engine that finds identical, similar, or contextually related images across its huge web index.

It has access to public social media, dating profiles, and online videos, so users can easily look up stolen stock or influencer photos.

While PimEyes focuses only on faces, Google analyzes locations, clothes, products, and more, with biographies, extra context, and no search limits.

\Google saves uploaded images to train its AI models by default. To prevent this, go to My Google Activity, open Search Services History, and turn Save Media off.

Test Results: From 59 Google results, 34 were accurate, with 22 linked to social media.
